subject: science
chapter_title: Exploration: Entering the World of Secondary Science

concepts.title: The Spirit of Scientific Exploration
concepts.definition: Secondary science moves from observing the world closely to testing ideas systematically: questions are sharpened into investigations, evidence is collected through experiments, and conclusions stay open to revision when new data arrive.
concepts.key_idea: Science at this stage is investigation, not memorisation: question, test, revise.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc101.txt opening sections (entering the world of secondary science)
question_patterns: how does secondary science differ from middle stage science
why do scientists revise their conclusions
what makes a question scientifically investigable
describe the steps of a scientific investigation
how do experiments provide evidence in science
give an example of a scientific idea that changed with new evidence

solution_steps.explain: Turn curiosity into a testable question.
Design experiments and record observations carefully.
State findings that stay open to new evidence.

concepts.title: Working Like a Scientist: Methods and Safety
concepts.definition: Scientific work combines careful observation, honest recording, control of variables and safe laboratory practice; measurements, tables and graphs organise evidence, and safety rules protect the investigator during every activity.
concepts.key_idea: Observation, controls, honest records and safety - the working habits of every scientist.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc101.txt sections on methods, recording and laboratory practice
question_patterns: why is controlling variables important in an experiment
list the safety rules to follow in a science laboratory
how do tables and graphs help in recording observations
what is a fair test in science
why must observations be recorded honestly
design a fair test for the given question

solution_steps.explain: Keep all but one variable fixed for a fair test.
Use tables, units and graphs for the data.
Follow laboratory safety rules during every activity.

concepts.title: Science in Society and Everyday Life
concepts.definition: Science connects classroom ideas to daily life and society - health, technology, agriculture and environment all carry scientific reasoning; understanding this link motivates exploration and responsible use of scientific knowledge.
concepts.key_idea: Everyday phenomena are science in action - and society needs scientific literacy.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc101.txt sections linking science with society and daily life
question_patterns: give two examples of science at work in your daily life
how does science help society solve problems
why is scientific literacy important for every citizen
connect a classroom concept to a technology you use
how can scientific knowledge be misused - discuss
which scientific question would you like to investigate and why

solution_steps.explain: Identify the concept hiding inside an everyday phenomenon.
Link the concept to technologies and social benefits.
Weigh ethical and environmental sides of applying knowledge.

questions: Describe the steps of a scientific investigation with an example.
Why are fair tests important in science?
Suggest one scientific question you would investigate and how.
